about: The spectator answer, version 2, of agentnexus-games-v1 under D-175: the version 1 answer and the provider's own clock facts, timing. Eight public matches, a scenario of viewer requests with the provider's answers, the answers every check must refuse, the frames of two streams, and how a viewer asks for each version. Test material only: every capability here is test bytes, valid nowhere. No contract version is published with this file.

steps.name: the-v2-snapshot
steps.because: The seat to move began its turn at 11:59:42, so its deadline is that instant plus 60 seconds, 42 seconds after the provider's clock. Connect Four has no match limit, so match_deadline_at is null.

steps.name: the-v2-events-after-3
steps.because: After, then answer=2, in that order: events 4 and 5, and the same timing rules.

steps.name: the-same-read-without-answer-is-the-v1-answer
steps.because: Without answer the answer is the version 1 answer, six members and no timing, byte for byte what version 1 gives. The provider has the clock facts and sends none of them.

steps.name: a-later-poll-keeps-the-deadline
steps.because: Reading again moves server_time and nothing else: the deadline is the stored start of the turn plus 60 seconds, never the time of the read.

steps.name: a-deadline-that-is-now
steps.because: The deadline equals server_time and the match is still active: valid. A deadline that has passed is not a timeout until a provider frame reports the match ended.

steps.name: a-deadline-one-second-ago
steps.because: One second after the deadline and still active: valid, because the provider enforces a deadline on its own tick. A spectator must not infer a result from it.

steps.name: the-opening-without-answer-is-the-published-v1-answer
steps.because: The bytes version 1 published for this match in vectors/spectator-v1, step a-read-from-the-observer, and nothing more.

steps.name: a-v2-read-from-the-observer
steps.because: The same read with answer=2 from the observer origin: the cross-origin header of version 1 and no other.

steps.name: a-preflight-for-the-v2-read
steps.because: No request header names the version, so the one preflight of D-139 is unchanged: it asks for GET with the capability header alone, and gets 204.

steps.name: a-write-to-the-v2-path
steps.because: A write is read_only on the version 2 path as on the version 1 path.

steps.name: the-v2-path-without-a-capability
steps.because: A read without a capability is unauthenticated, and says no more.

steps.name: an-unstarted-match
steps.because: A Chess match is awaiting_seats until both seats are bound: no turn and no limit runs, so both deadlines are null, never absent.

steps.name: an-ended-match
steps.because: The match has ended: both deadlines are null, although the provider still holds the start of the last turn.

steps.name: a-seat-that-has-not-bound
steps.because: The match is active and it is the second seat's turn, but that seat has not bound: no timer runs for a role without a bound seat, so turn_deadline_at is null.

steps.name: a-chess-match-right-after-a-move
steps.because: A move was accepted this second, so the turn deadline is 60 seconds ahead. The Chess limit, activation plus 50 minutes, is 34 minutes 38 seconds ahead.

steps.name: an-active-chess-match
steps.because: Twenty seconds later the turn deadline has not moved and 40 seconds remain; the match limit is 34 minutes 18 seconds ahead.

steps.name: an-aborted-match
steps.because: The 50-minute limit ended the match aborted, with no winner: both deadlines are null. The limit is the provider's, never a result.

refused_answers.name: no-timing
refused_answers.because: The answer has no timing: it is a version 1 answer, which version 2 does not accept.

refused_answers.name: timing-is-null
refused_answers.because: timing is required and is an object; null is not a way to say there is no clock.

refused_answers.name: timing-without-server-time
refused_answers.because: All three members are required.

refused_answers.name: timing-without-turn-deadline-at
refused_answers.because: A deadline that does not apply is null, never absent.

refused_answers.name: timing-without-match-deadline-at
refused_answers.because: A deadline that does not apply is null, never absent.

refused_answers.name: timing-with-an-extra-member
refused_answers.because: timing is closed: a fixed object, not a map of metadata.

refused_answers.name: timing-with-the-capability-expiry
refused_answers.because: The capability's expiry is separate: it never travels in timing.

refused_answers.name: an-extra-member-next-to-timing
refused_answers.because: The answer stays closed: server_time belongs inside timing.

refused_answers.name: server-time-with-a-space-for-the-t
refused_answers.because: server_time: A space where the T belongs.

refused_answers.name: server-time-with-an-offset
refused_answers.because: server_time: An offset is not canonical UTC: the Z is literal.

refused_answers.name: server-time-with-a-fraction
refused_answers.because: server_time: Whole seconds only: no fraction.

refused_answers.name: server-time-in-lower-case-z
refused_answers.because: server_time: The Z is upper case.

refused_answers.name: server-time-as-a-number
refused_answers.because: server_time: An instant is a string, not a number.

refused_answers.name: server-time-empty
refused_answers.because: server_time: An empty string is not an instant.

refused_answers.name: turn-deadline-with-a-fraction
refused_answers.because: turn_deadline_at: whole seconds only, no fraction.

refused_answers.name: turn-deadline-as-a-number
refused_answers.because: turn_deadline_at: an instant is a string, not a number.

refused_answers.name: match-deadline-with-an-offset
refused_answers.because: match_deadline_at: an offset is not canonical UTC.

refused_answers.name: match-deadline-empty
refused_answers.because: match_deadline_at: an empty string is not an instant, and not null.

refused_answers.name: ended-keeps-a-turn-deadline
refused_answers.because: A match that has ended has no running turn.

refused_answers.name: ended-keeps-a-match-deadline
refused_answers.because: A match that has ended has no running limit.

refused_answers.name: aborted-keeps-a-turn-deadline
refused_answers.because: A match that has been aborted has no running turn.

refused_answers.name: aborted-keeps-a-match-deadline
refused_answers.because: A match that has been aborted has no running limit.

refused_answers.name: awaiting-seats-keeps-a-turn-deadline
refused_answers.because: A match that has not started has no running turn.

refused_answers.name: awaiting-seats-keeps-a-match-deadline
refused_answers.because: A match that has not started has no running limit.

refused_answers.name: connect-four-with-a-match-deadline
refused_answers.because: Connect Four has no active-match limit: match_deadline_at is null, never a made-up limit.

refused_answers.name: connect-four-solo-with-a-match-deadline
refused_answers.because: The rule is for every game version that begins connect-four-, solo included.

refused_answers.name: a-turn-deadline-61-seconds-ahead
refused_answers.because: A turn never begins in the future, so its deadline is at most 60 seconds after server_time.

refused_answers.name: the-two-deadlines-swapped
refused_answers.because: The match limit sits in the turn's place and the turn's in the limit's: 3000 seconds ahead is more than a turn can be.

refused_answers.name: a-match-deadline-3001-seconds-ahead
refused_answers.because: A match never began in the future, so its limit is at most 50 minutes after server_time.

refused_answers.name: an-active-chess-match-without-a-match-deadline
refused_answers.because: An active Chess match has its limit running, so match_deadline_at is not null.

refused_answers.name: a-timestamp-that-is-no-instant
refused_answers.because: The shape is canonical and there is no 30 February: the pattern is the schema's, the calendar is the check's.

refused_answers.name: a-view-that-is-not-the-games
refused_answers.because: The snapshot is not the game version's spectator view: it names a member the view does not.

streams.name: a-connect-four-match-to-its-end
streams.because: Three frames: the snapshot on connect, then one frame for each event committed. Each has its own server_time; a move starts a fresh 60 seconds for the other seat; the last frame shows the end and no deadline.

streams.name: a-chess-match-to-its-end
streams.because: Five frames. The fourth carries two events, plies 6 and 7, because both were committed before it was built; every other later frame carries one. The match limit stays where activation put it until the last frame, which shows the draw and no deadline.

negotiation.about: How a viewer asks for each version over HTTP and over a stream, what a provider that implements only version 1 may do with answer=2, and what a viewer then holds. The capability is the same for both versions and for both ways.

requests.name: answer-2
requests.because: The one way to ask for version 2.

requests.name: after-3-and-answer-2
requests.because: With a cursor: after first, answer last.

requests.name: no-query
requests.because: No answer, so the version 1 answer.

requests.name: after-3
requests.because: A cursor alone is a version 1 request.

requests.name: answer-1
requests.because: Only answer=2 asks for a version; 1 is refused.

requests.name: answer-02
requests.because: The value is exactly 2, with no zero before it.

requests.name: after-3-and-answer-2-twice
requests.because: A repeated answer is refused after a cursor too.

requests.name: an-unknown-parameter
requests.because: The version 1 reference check refuses a query it does not know. That is the reference check's strictness; a provider that ignores a parameter other than answer is not in conflict with this text.

requests.name: answer-2-and-an-unknown-parameter
requests.because: The reference check serves exactly the two forms.

stream.name: v2-offer-to-a-provider-with-both
stream.because: A provider that implements version 2 selects it.

stream.name: v1-offer-to-a-provider-with-both
stream.because: The version 1 offer keeps version 1 frames.

stream.name: v2-offer-to-a-v1-only-provider
stream.because: A provider that implements only version 1 refuses before the stream opens: its first subprotocol must be agentnexus-watch-v1.

stream.name: v1-offer-to-a-v1-only-provider
stream.because: The viewer then offers version 1 once more, on a new connection.

stream.name: the-capability-before-v2
stream.because: The version is first, the capability second.

stream.name: v1-without-the-capability
stream.because: Exactly two subprotocols, as in version 1.

stream.name: v1-and-v2
stream.because: The second is the capability, not a version.

v1_only_provider.about: A provider that implements only version 1 does not know answer. It may ignore the parameter and answer with the plain version 1 answer (ignoring), or refuse the request as it refuses any query it does not know (refusing). A viewer that asked for version 2 accepts both. The answer it may get back is a valid version 1 answer and is not a valid version 2 answer, so the schemas alone tell the two apart.

requests.name: answer-2-to-a-provider-that-implements-only-version-1
requests.because: The version 1 answer, as if answer were not there: no timing, so no numeric clock.

requests.name: after-3-and-answer-2-to-a-provider-that-implements-only-version-1
requests.because: The same with a cursor: the version 1 answer with events 4 and 5.
